data.name: Jul
data.gender_notes: Jul is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The diminutive form of Julius, meaning 'downy-headed' or 'youthful'. The name Jul carries the meaning “Short, little, young” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Jul usually hope their child will grow to embody short, little, young and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings, growth, and the joy of youth.
data.etymology: Jul belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Short, little, young.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jul total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Jul" in its original form, Julius, has a significant cultural impact in the Roman tradition. Julius was a legendary Roman king according to legend, and several of Rome's most renowned figures, including Julius Caesar and Gaius Julius Caesar Octavianus (later known as Augustus), bore this name.
data.spiritual_significance: In an Islamic context, the spiritual significance of the name "Jul" is connected to lily flowers. Jul and Joul are variants of the name Julian, which shares the same root as the Arabic word for lily (al-raghbiya), making the name symbolically related to this delicate, beautiful flower. Lily flowers are associated with purity, innocence, and rebirth in many cultures and religious traditions, making "Jul" an evocative name that carries a sense of spiritual refinement and renewal.
